definition: In artificial intelligence and cloud computing, compute is the amount of computing power or computational resources required to train large language models.
details: More broadly, compute is the computational power or resources necessary for a computer or computer program to function.

explainer.lead: Compute is the computing power and resources a program needs to run. In AI, it often refers specifically to what is needed to train large language models, making it a basic practical constraint on that work.

tiers.eli5: Compute is like the energy and kitchen space needed to cook a meal: a bigger meal needs more of both. Training a large language model is a very big computing job, so it needs a lot of computing power and resources.
tiers.practitioner: When planning large language model training, compute describes the computing power and resources the workload requires. A common pitfall is treating it as a synonym for one particular chip or as an AI-only term; more broadly, it applies to any computer or computer program.
tiers.paperLevel: Compute denotes the computational power or resources necessary for a computer or computer program to function. In the narrower AI usage, it is the amount required to train large language models; the term itself does not specify a unit or formula.

explainer.example: A team training a large language model needs substantial computing power and resources for the training run. That required capacity is its compute; a less demanding program can function with less.

usedIn.name: Large language model training
usedIn.detail: Compute describes the resources required to carry out the training workload.

usedIn.name: Cloud computing
usedIn.detail: The term is used for the computing power and resources needed by computational work.

usedIn.name: General computing
usedIn.detail: More broadly, compute covers what a computer or program needs to function.

explainer.intuition: Think of compute as the computational capacity a task demands. Bigger or more demanding tasks require more of it, just as bigger physical jobs require more labor or equipment.
howItWorks: Start with a computational task, such as running a program or training a large language model.
Identify the computing power and resources that the task needs.
Describe that required amount as the task's compute.
Compare tasks by recognizing that more demanding workloads require more compute.
explainer.whyItMatters: Compute connects an AI training goal with the practical resources needed to pursue it. It also provides a broad way to discuss computational requirements beyond AI.
misconceptions: Compute is not exclusively an AI term; it applies to computers and programs generally.
Compute does not name a particular machine, chip, unit, or formula.
In its narrower AI usage, compute concerns the resources required for training large language models.
